synthesis_narrative: The literature grounding this work contains complementary technical threads. The "STaRK" benchmark establishes the concrete problem setting—heterogeneous, text-rich KGs and an entity-level Hit@1/MRR evaluation—that motivates methods which must balance global coverage and multi-hop relational reasoning. From the LLM agent side, "ReAct" formalized interleaving model reasoning with external tool actions, giving a template for exposing a small, prompt-specified toolset to control retrieval behavior. On the graph-traversal front, methods such as "Tree-of-Traversals" and "Think-on-Graph" concretely demonstrate multi-hop exploration policies but also reveal critical failure modes: dependence on seed selection and fixed hop strategies that cause anchoring and missed evidence. Complementing traversal work, hybrid retrievers like "HybGRAG" show how combining semantic retrieval and local graph signals improves coverage yet typically remain static scoring pipelines that cannot dynamically switch search modes. Finally, practical compression techniques from "Distilling Interactive Policies via Label-free Trajectory Imitation" provide an operational recipe for taking costly teacher interactions and producing a compact, label-free student model. Together these threads expose a clear opportunity: combine persistent global discovery with composable one-hop expansion under a promptable tool interface and then compress the resulting adaptive policy. The current paper naturally follows by implementing a minimal two-tool LLM agent that alternates breadth and depth without seed dependence, evaluates on "STaRK", and uses label-free trajectory distillation to yield an efficient distilled retriever.
